title.en: The President and Vice-President of India
The house in Delhi, the retreat in Shimla

text.en: The President of India lives in Rashtrapati Bhavan in New Delhi, but must also work at least once a year from the Retreat in Shimla in the north and Rashtrapati Nilayam in Hyderabad in the south. The three places symbolise one country with many cultures.

The Central Government has three organs, the Union Executive, the Legislature known as Parliament, and the Judiciary headed by the Supreme Court.
Articles 52 to 78 in Part V of the Constitution deal with the Union Executive.
The President is the nominal executive and the first citizen, as well as Supreme Commander of the armed forces.
He is elected by an electoral college of the elected members of both Houses of Parliament, of the states, and of Delhi and Puducherry, by proportional representation with the single transferable vote.
To stand for President a person must be an Indian citizen aged at least 35, hold no office of profit, and be proposed by 50 electors and seconded by 50 more.
The term is five years, and he may be re-elected, taking his oath before the Chief Justice of India.
Executive powers: he appoints the Prime Minister, Governors, judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, the Attorney General, CAG, Chief Election Commissioner and ambassadors.
Legislative powers: he summons Parliament at least twice a year, may dissolve the Lok Sabha, gives assent to bills, and nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.
A Money Bill cannot be introduced without his approval, and the Contingency Fund of India is at his disposal.
Article 72 gives him the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions, or to commute a sentence.
He can proclaim National Emergency under Article 352, State Emergency under Article 356, and Financial Emergency under Article 360.
He may be removed by impeachment under Article 61 for violating the Constitution.
The Vice-President, elected for five years by indirect election, is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and acts as President for up to six months when needed.
He may cast a vote in the Rajya Sabha only to break a tie, and if both posts are vacant, the Chief Justice acts, as M. Hidayatullah did in 1969.

problem.en: List the powers of the President of India.

text.en: Executive: he appoints the Prime Minister, Governors and judges.

why.en: Every action is taken in his name.

text.en: Legislative: he summons Parliament and assents to bills.

why.en: He nominates 12 members to the Rajya Sabha.

text.en: Judicial, military, financial and emergency powers.

why.en: Article 72 pardon, Supreme Commander, Contingency Fund, Articles 352, 356 and 360.

prompt.en: Who elects the President and what is the term?

requiredIdeas.en: Electoral college of elected MPs and MLAs

commonMisconceptions.en: Saying the people elect the President directly

points.en: President: nominal executive, first citizen, five years.
Powers: executive, legislative, financial, judicial, military, diplomatic, emergency.
Vice-President: Chairman of Rajya Sabha, casting vote.
